_measurement_definitions.distinct_compounds: COUNT(DISTINCT molregno) FROM chembl_v.bioactivities_by_accession WHERE accession=<ACC> AND n_target_components = 1. The n_target_components=1 predicate is LOAD-BEARING and is the single most common way to get these numbers wrong — see _audit_2026_08_15.
_measurement_definitions.total_activities: COUNT(*) over the same view with the same n_target_components = 1 predicate.
_measurement_definitions.best_potency_nm: MAX(pchembl_value) over the same filtered set, converted 10^(9-pchembl), AND THEN rejected if the source assay description is uncharacterised per CLAUDE.md rule 6 ('Inhibition of X (unknown origin)', 'Binding affinity to X (unknown origin)'). Where the raw maximum is rejected on that ground the entry says so explicitly. standard_relation must be '='.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_total: COUNT(DISTINCT entry_id) FROM pdb_v.structures_by_accession WHERE accession=<ACC>. NOTE: this view has one row per (accession, entry, entity), so COUNT(*) overcounts — KRAS is 534 rows for 522 entries.
_measurement_definitions._STRUCTURE_AXIS_REGENERATED_2026_08_15: Every pdb_holo / pdb_apo / pdb_undetermined figure below was REGENERATED WHOLESALE on 2026-08-15 under the definition in `pdb_holo`. Nothing was patched. The prior values were produced by the superseded '250-1200 Da + $EXCL' MW-window rule, and before that by '>=300 Da'. Both are gone. Where a regenerated count disagrees with an earlier adjudication, the disagreement is recorded ON THE TARGET rather than reconciled away — see `_structure_regeneration_2026_08_15`.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_holo: CHEMISTRY CLASSIFIER, not a molecular-weight window. An entry is HOLO iff at least one of its components in pdb_v.entry_ligands classifies as `druglike` under `.claude/skills/structure-select/ligand_filter.py::classify_record`. Measured 2026-08-15. Classifier sha256 ae9ef140f3f8b8109a9384e287aa67a4a2ab130443a6144247c12def0b5216c1, 2430 lines, tunables LIPID_MIN_CHAIN=8 / TRIVIAL_MAX_HEAVY_ATOMS=9 / DRUGLIKE_MAX_MW=1200. SEE `_classifier_pin_corrected_2026_08_15` — the sha256 previously recorded here did not identify any file in this checkout. `classify_record` takes a pdb_v.entry_ligands row verbatim and does NO I/O, so every verdict here is reproducible offline from the row. THERE IS NO LOWER MW BOUND ANY MORE — that is the single biggest behavioural change and it is deliberate: the module's own comment says the old 18-heavy-atom floor 'is gone, because size was never the discriminator', and the floor was demonstrably splitting congeneric series across the holo/apo line.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_apo: an entry with NO `druglike` component AND NO `unknown` component. Strictly narrower than 'not holo'.
_measurement_definitions.pdb_undetermined: an entry with no `druglike` component but at least one component the classifier returned `unknown` for. THIS IS NOT APO AND MUST NEVER BE ADDED TO THE APO COUNT. `unknown` has two causes and both are live in this file: (a) the CCD names the component 'UNKNOWN LIGAND' / unidentified density — TYK2 5C01 carries `UNL`; (b) the component exceeds the 1200 Da ceiling and no cofactor/lipid/peptide signature fired, so the classifier refuses rather than assumes — BCL-2 8FY1 and 8FY2. A third cause, a Paperclip lookup FAILURE, carries the `lookup_failed` flag into holo_call(...)['undetermined'] and is a network fact, not a chemistry fact. pdb_total = pdb_holo + pdb_apo + pdb_undetermined, always.
known_limits_of_the_new_holo_rule: FALSE POSITIVE, measured here and NOT in the classifier's own test set: TNF-alpha 5UUI's MTN (MTSL nitroxide spin label, 264 Da, covalently attached to an engineered T77C cysteine) classifies `druglike`. Its chemistry genuinely is drug-like; what disqualifies it is the entry title ('Crystal Structure of Spin-Labeled T77C TNFa'), which no chemistry test can see. The module's docstring claims 0 false positives on a 70-component held-out sample; that claim is about that sample and MTN was not in it. Chemistry alone cannot catch a covalent biophysical probe.

FALSE NEGATIVE, declared by the module and live here: nucleoside/SAM-analog inhibitors classify `cofactor`. STAT3 5AX3's 5ID (a 7-deazaadenosine, 5-iodotubercidin class) is a real nucleoside-analog inhibitor filed as a cofactor. This is why STAT3 moves 3 -> 2. The bias is deliberate and conservative: a false negative costs one holo structure, a false positive invents one.

DEGRADERS ARE ONLY HALF-CAUGHT, and the half that fails does so silently. MEASURED on BCL-2 2026-08-15, not assumed. The 1200 Da ceiling works as advertised: 8FY1's YF8 (1640 Da) returns `unknown` and lands in pdb_undetermined, visible as unresolved. But 8FY2's YFH (1682 Da) NEVER REACHES THE CEILING — rule R10 fires first, because `peptide_backbone_residues()` counts three alpha-amino-acid backbone units in the degrader's linker and amide-rich warhead, so the classifier returns `peptide_or_polymer` and the entry is counted APO with no flag and nothing for a reader to notice. PROTACs and molecular glues are amide-rich by construction, so this misfires across the whole modality and it misfires quietly. Inspect `peptide_or_polymer` verdicts above ~1000 Da by hand; filter on the `standalone_peptide_ligand` flag R10 sets. This limitation was NOT in the module's declared false-negative list.
drugbank_id is not a druglikeness signal and does not gate anything — MTN carries DB08217. The classifier reads the field but never lets it decide.

The hand-written $EXCL comp_id list is NO LONGER USED for these counts. It is reproduced by the classifier's chemistry without having been shown it, and its two documented leaks (MTN; RORgt 4NIE's DMX = NDSB-256 sulfobetaine) are now handled on chemistry — DMX is caught, MTN is not.
_measurement_definitions.how_to_reproduce_and_the_trap_that_will_: Pull pdb_v.entry_ligands for the accession's entries, call classify_record per distinct comp_id, and count entries. THE TRAP IS NOT CHEMISTRY, IT IS PAGING. Paperclip's documented row cap is 200 but the SERVED cap moves under load: on 2026-08-15 the identical entry-list query returned 200 rows at one moment and EXACTLY 10 at another, with no error and a well-formed table both times. A short page is therefore ambiguous between 'end of results' and 'silently truncated', and OFFSET paging under-counts without ever failing. The first run of this regeneration recorded KRAS as 10 entries against a true 522 and would have written it into this grading key as a measurement. EVERY count in this file was re-taken by paging at whatever page size RECONCILES with an independently issued COUNT aggregate, bracketed by a canary on both pdb_v tables (TNF-alpha = 52 entries; 4OBE apo / 6OIM holo on MOV per structure-select SKILL.md §1). A count that does not reconcile is not recorded.

_TWO_NEW_PAPERCLIP_FAILURE_SIGNATURES_20._what: CLAUDE.md rule 15 enumerates FOUR Paperclip failure signatures. MEASURED WHILE REGENERATING KRAS AND EGFR, THERE ARE AT LEAST SIX. Both new ones are silent, both corrupt data rather than blocking it, and NEITHER is caught by reconciling row counts against a COUNT aggregate — which is what rule 14 relies on. Recorded here because the fixture counts in this file depend on them being handled. CLAUDE.md is not this fixture set's to edit; rule 15's table needs two more rows and rule 14 needs the caveat below.
_TWO_NEW_PAPERCLIP_FAILURE_SIGNATURES_20.signature_5_SILENT_PER_COLUMN_TRUNCATION: THE DANGEROUS ONE, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE MOVING ROW CAP. In normal full-row mode, a long column value is truncated at 80 characters with NO ellipsis, NO marker, and NO error. Caught only by selecting LENGTH(smiles) beside smiles: component A1AHB returned 80 characters against a server-side LENGTH() of 100. WHY THIS BEATS EVERY EXISTING GUARD: the row COUNT is correct, so rule 14's reconciliation passes cleanly; the truncated value is still syntactically valid SMILES, so it PARSES; and classify_record therefore returns a CONFIDENT WRONG VERDICT rather than an error or an `unknown`. A capped row set at least yields a number you can catch. This yields a wrong verdict that looks exactly like a right one. WORKAROUND USED FOR KRAS AND EGFR: fetch SMILES as five 50-character SUBSTRINGs, reassemble, and assert the reassembled length against a server-side LENGTH() for every component — done for all 527 components across both targets, all reconciled. COROLLARY THAT INVALIDATES A SHORTCUT THIS FILE AND CLAUDE.md RULE 14 BOTH RECOMMEND: `STRING_AGG(DISTINCT comp_id,' ') GROUP BY entry_id` hits the same 80-char cap and SILENTLY DROPS COMPONENTS off multi-ligand entries, which would misfile a holo entry as apo whenever its druglike component sorted late. Rule 14 clause 4 advises server-side aggregation as the way to never need reconciliation — that advice is correct about ROW caps and WRONG about this one. It was abandoned for KRAS/EGFR in favour of paging raw DISTINCT (entry_id, comp_id) pairs. CHECKED FOR THE TARGETS ALREADY MEASURED WITH IT: IL-17A's longest aggregate is 10 characters (max 3 components per entry) and RORgt's is 18 (max 5), both far below 80, so those counts are unaffected — verified rather than assumed.
_TWO_NEW_PAPERCLIP_FAILURE_SIGNATURES_20.signature_6_DISPLAY_PREVIEW_CAP_DISTINCT: At LIMIT 100 the CLI prints `Preview (first 5 of 100 rows)` plus a `Too many rows (100) for context` hint, while the footer STILL TRUTHFULLY READS `(100 rows, 12ms)` and the column header is complete. So len(parsed_rows) = 5 while the footer says 100. This is an output-SIZE budget, not a row count, so a WIDER select trips it at a LOWER row count — meaning a page size that worked for a narrow query will silently under-deliver for a wide one. Verify the parsed row count per page against the footer, rather than trusting a page size that worked before. Distinct from the moving 200/10 row cap in rule 14.
_TWO_NEW_PAPERCLIP_FAILURE_SIGNATURES_20.also_observed: `[waiting] Too many concurrent requests (max 10). Retrying in Ns` under parallel load — benign and self-retrying, but it can push a call past its own statement timeout and surface as signature 1. And `[error] Request timed out` fired on a trivial MAX(LENGTH(...)) aggregate that had succeeded seconds earlier, confirming rule 15's note that the timeout carries no information about query cost. All transient; short-then-long retry cleared each on attempt 2.

backend_failures.1_moving_row_cap: Paperclip's documented cap is 200 rows. The SERVED cap moved to EXACTLY 10 under load, with no error and a well-formed table. backend_failures.3_the_endpoint_is_shared_and_capped_at_1: Another client on the same box held 15-21 connections for much of this task. `paperclip` handles the limit itself with up to five backoffs, so a SHORT outer timeout is actively harmful — it kills the client mid-backoff and re-launches it. backend_failures.4_tool_level_breakage: Late in the task every `paperclip sql` began returning `vsh: cd: /papers/: Permission denied` in ~17 ms — not a timeout, a broken tool. `paperclip search` was unaffected. This is what stopped the last five targets.

method_validation.pdb_holo_grading: RESOLVED 2026-08-15: THE GRADED CRITERION ON THIS TARGET IS NOT A SCALAR. Grade the DISPOSITION OF 8FY1 AND 8FY2, not the integer. Both 39 and 41 PASS when the agent states what it did with the two degrader co-crystals; a bare integer FAILS at every value, 39 and 41 included. That is the resolution, and the argument is below.
method_validation.pdb_holo_grading_the_argument: The previous key graded 39 and 'also accepted' 39/40/41. That is a defect in two directions and both were live. (1) It penalised the better answer by relegating it to a tolerance band: 41 is the DEFENSIBLE count — 39 plus the two bivalent degrader co-crystals, which are real beyond-rule-of-5 small-molecule precedent that a scientist counting BCL-2 precedent should count — and grading 39 makes the better science merely forgiven rather than rewarded. (2) But simply flipping the graded value to 41 fails the other way: an agent that runs classify_record exactly as this file specifies GETS 39, and marking it wrong for correctly operating the specified tool would punish compliance and teach agents to hand-adjust tool output toward an expected number, which is a far worse habit than an off-by-two count. Both scalars are defensible and NEITHER is the thing worth measuring. What actually separates a good dossier from a bad one here is whether the agent SAW the two entries at all — so grade that. An agent reporting 39 'plus 8FY1 undetermined and 8FY2 misfiled peptide_or_polymer, both real degrader precedent' and an agent reporting 41 'counting both degraders' have done the SAME work and both pass. An agent reporting a bare 41 has not done better science than one reporting a bare 39; it has produced a number this key cannot distinguish from luck.
method_validation.pdb_holo_grading_what_to_reject: REJECT a bare number at any value — 39, 40, 41 — because both degraders are invisible in a bare number and 8FY2 is invisible even in its verdict, so a bare number is not evidence the agent looked. REJECT 40 outright even when the disposition is stated: 40 is the SUPERSEDED 250-1200 Da + $EXCL MW-window value and is unreachable under the chemistry classifier this file mandates. Reaching it means a retracted rule was used, and the previous key's acceptance of it was a straightforward error — it rewarded the rule the regeneration exists to abolish. REJECT any count that adds 8FY1 to pdb_apo: `unknown` is not apo, and pdb_total = pdb_holo + pdb_apo + pdb_undetermined always.
method_validation.pdb_holo_grading_the_generalisable_findi: The reason to grade the disposition rather than the integer is not special pleading for BCL-2. 8FY2 is a POSITIVE misclassification, not a refusal — no flag, no `unknown`, nothing for a reader to notice — and PROTAC and molecular-glue degraders are amide-rich by construction, so this misfires across the whole modality and it misfires QUIETLY. A key that grades the integer cannot tell an agent that inspected the peptide_or_polymer bucket from one that did not. A key that grades the disposition can. Any target whose count depends on a silent classifier limitation should be graded the same way.

method_validation.distinct_compounds_the_coincidence_that_: THE REASON THIS PAIR LOOKED IRRECONCILABLE FOR SO LONG IS A NUMERIC COLLISION, AND IT IS WORTH NAMING BECAUSE IT WILL RECUR. 1,249 is simultaneously (a) MYC's compound count WITHOUT the n_target_components=1 predicate and (b) MYC's activity count WITH it. Two different measurements on two different axes that land on the same integer. So the sweep table's '1,249 compounds' and this file's '1,249 activities' look like the same figure filed under two names, or like one of them being a copy error — and neither is true. immunology.pdb_holo_THE_PREDICTION_THIS_FILE_MADE_W: MEASURED, AND THE _NOT_REGENERATED NOTE'S PREDICTION FAILED ON THE HALF IT WAS MOST CONFIDENT ABOUT. That note predicted 4NIE's DMX (NDSB-256) 'should now be CAUGHT' by the Good's-buffer rule. IT IS NOT. DMX classifies `druglike`. A C3-symmetric triol on a C3-symmetric trimer axis is the shape of a designed probe, not of a buffer component, and no cofactor/lipid/additive signature fires. But it is a bare polyol with no nitrogen, the paper was not retrieved, and 'designed for the 3-fold axis' is an inference. Counted in the 20; an agent that rejects it and reports 18 with 38A named has NOT made an error.

6OOY.verdict: REAL — confirmed again. The des-pyridyl parent of a series deposited the same day: A6Y (343 Da, 6OOZ) and A7A (424 Da, 6OP0). Uncontested across all four rules.

backup_structure_regenerated.note: STAT3 MOVES 3 -> 2, and the delta is a DECLARED FALSE NEGATIVE of the classifier, not a data change. Only three STAT3 entries carry any component at all: 6NJS and 6NUQ both carry KQV (836 Da, druglike — counted), and 5AX3 carries 5ID, a 392 Da 7-deazaadenosine of the 5-iodotubercidin class. 5ID is a real nucleoside-analog inhibitor, but the classifier files every purine-plus-ribose as `cofactor` — its docstring names this exact class as a known false negative ('a purine plus a ribose is the nucleotide signature whether or not a medicinal chemist made it'). So 2 is what the rule produces and 3 is defensible on the chemistry. ACCEPT EITHER when 5AX3/5ID is named; the failure mode to catch is reporting 3 without noticing that one of the three is a nucleoside. This does not disturb the backup's role — 'thin structural evidence' is if anything more true at 2 than at 3.

slot_6_recent_orphan.best_potency_rejected_note: REJECTED 2026-08-15 UNDER THIS FILE'S OWN RULE, and this was an internal inconsistency, not a data change. `_measurement_definitions.best_potency_nm` says a value is rejected 'if the source assay description is uncharacterised per CLAUDE.md rule 6 ("Inhibition of X (unknown origin)", "Binding affinity to X (unknown origin)")'. IL-11's own `assay_provenance` field, three lines above, records the description as 'Binding affinity to CAP chip-immobilized IL-11 (UNKNOWN ORIGIN) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis'. That is the second forbidden pattern, verbatim. The file applied rule 6 to KRAS — where it explicitly declines to raise the potency to 0.020 nM on exactly this ground — and did not apply it here. No query was needed to see this; it is provable from the file against itself. The two numbers are retained above because they are real rows and an agent WILL find them, which is the temptation this fixture exists to pose; what changes is that the grading key no longer asserts either as a potency.
